subject: ACME RAG eval — retrieval & reranker follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Sullivan <erin.sullivan@acme.com>, Tom Chen <tom.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: ACME RAG eval — retrieval & reranker follow-up

Hi Erin / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery + demo and proposed next steps so we’re all aligned: 

Call recap:
- Goal: Improve help-center search and automated response accuracy for ACME product docs and troubleshooting guides; reduce escalations to support.
- Current pain: high hallucination rate on long-form answers and inconsistent grounding for recent KB content.
- Success metrics discussed: P@1 for top answer, nDCG@5, and grounding rate (fraction of answers with direct doc citations).

Preliminary recommendations (high level):
- Retriever: hybrid setup (BM25 cold start + vector-based ANN on embeddings index). Start with top_k=50 retrieval, then rerank to top_10.
- Embeddings model: text-embedding-3-large for initial runs (good balance of accuracy/cost); we can try a smaller embedding if cost needs tighten.
- Reranker: two-stage test — lightweight bi-encoder (fast) vs cross-encoder reranker (higher quality). For baseline, we recommend cross-encoder-reranker-v2 for ACME since quality is the priority.
- Generation: Redwood-Chat-Opt-13B (constrained decoding + grounding prompts) for current evals; we can test a 7B option if latency/cost constraints tighten.

I attached the initial benchmark CSV and the prompt set we used in today’s demo. Please review the prompts (prompt_set_v2.md) and let us know any domain-specific adjustments.

Suggested next steps / asks:
1) Approve a 48-hour run of the full retrieval+reranker baseline against your canonical KB (we’ll spin on a copy of your index you shared). This will produce P@1, nDCG@5, grounding rate, and latency percentiles.
2) Marissa to share retrieval hyperparameters and the reranker config (attached).
3) ACME: confirm which KB slices (docs + tickets vs docs-only) to include in the baseline.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to review results and align on rollout plan.

Proposed times: Wed Jul 21 9:00–11:00 PT or Thu Jul 22 13:00–15:00 PT — let me know what works.

Files attached: acme_benchmark_results.csv, prompt_set_v2.md, redwood_reranker_recs.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Marissa — great session. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we approve the 48-hour run:

1) Latency SLOs: what latency should we expect for the cross-encoder reranker path (p95 for a single query) when running top_k=50 then rerank top_10? We need to be sure we can hit <600ms for interactive responses.
2) Cost estimate: can you share a rough per-query cost delta between the bi-encoder-only path and the cross-encoder path? We’ll use that in the procurement evaluation.
3) Data retention/compliance: we prefer a 30-day ephemeral log retention for PII reasons — does your test run honor that by default?

We’re happy to proceed if these are within expectations. Also, for the KB slice — start with docs-only for the first run; we’ll add tickets after we see initial grounding numbers.

—Erin
Erin Sullivan
Head of Search & Knowledge 
ACME Corp
erin.sullivan@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Sullivan <erin.sullivan@acme.com>
Cc: Tom Chen <tom.chen@acme.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ACME RAG eval — retrieval & reranker follow-up

Erin — thanks for the questions. Answers below and a few more details that should help procurement/security.

1) Latency expectations (cross-encoder reranker path):
- Retrieval (FAISS HNSW; top_k=50): ~15–40 ms p50/p95 depending on index size and replica config.
- Bi-encoder scoring + ANN: ~25–60 ms p95 for embeddings lookup when using text-embedding-3-large.
- Cross-encoder reranker (rerank top_10, batch size tunable): ~200–450 ms p95 on a single A100-equivalent GPU when using batch size=8 and optimized kernels.
- Total expected p95: ~300–550 ms in our internal runs (for typical KB sizes). We can likely hit <600ms p95 with right parallelism and a tuned batch size.

2) Cost delta (rough):
- Bi-encoder only flow (retrieve via ANN + generate): baseline cost X per 1k queries.
- Cross-encoder path (retrieve 50 -> cross-encode top_10 -> generate): ~2.5–3x the per-query compute cost vs bi-encoder-only (vector lookup + generator) for the reranker portion. Exact $/token depends on model and quantization profile; Marcus will follow up with a punched-out cost spreadsheet.

3) Data retention/compliance:
- Test runs honor customer-specified retention; we can configure ephemeral logs (30 days) and ensure no customer PII is persisted beyond that for the eval. We’ll run on a private test index copy.

Additional notes on evaluation metrics and test plan:
- Metrics we’ll compute: Precision@1, nDCG@5, Grounding Rate (percentage of outputs with at least one doc citation), Hallucination Rate (annotated samples), Latency percentiles (p50/p95), and Cost per successful query.
- Reranker A/B plan: run 48 hours with two arms: (A) bi-encoder-only + generator (fast), (B) retrieve top_50 -> cross-encoder-rerank top_10 -> generator. We’ll keep generator and prompts fixed to isolate reranker impact.
- Ground truth: we’ll use your canonical docs-only testset and a small human-annotated sample (n=500) for hallucination labeling.

I’ve uploaded the full run config, prompts, and the recommended reranker tuning (redwood_reranker_recs.pdf) to the ACME folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AcmeRagEval

Next steps (per your note to start docs-only):
- Marissa / Marcus: kick off 48-hour A/B baseline against docs-only copy once Erin confirms.
- Marcus: produce cost delta spreadsheet + expected infra footprint.
- David: produce a short note on retention/config options for security (30-day ephemeral).

If that sounds good, Erin — confirm and we’ll schedule Wed 9:30 PT to review initial results (I penciled it in).

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: ACME RAG eval — internal action items (follow-up)

Folks — quick internal follow-up from the ACME thread above. ACME confirmed docs-only baseline and asked the latency/cost clarifications which we answered. They tentatively agreed to Wed 9:30 PT — I scheduled but will confirm after Marcus posts infra notes.

Action items:
- Marcus: kick off the 48-hour A/B baseline (two arms: bi-encoder-only vs cross-encoder-reranker) on the docs-only copy. Config: FAISS HNSW index, text-embedding-3-large, top_k=50 retrieval, rerank top_10. Store raw logs to the run bucket and share path. Target start: Today EOD PST.
- Marcus: export p50/p95 latency histograms and a sample (n=500) of retriever + reranker scored candidates for annotation.
- David: produce a 1-page cost delta estimate (dollars per 1k queries) for both arms, with assumptions (GPU type, instance count, token rates). Also draft the retention/config note for security (30-day ephemeral logs).
- Marissa: coordinate with ACME to confirm Wed 9:30 PT meeting and share the human-annotation plan.

Notes for the run:
- For the reranker, start with cross-encoder-reranker-v2 with batch_size=8, but keep the pipeline flexible to swap to a distilled cross-encoder if p95 exceeds 600ms.
- Log the grounding indicators we discussed (citation span, doc_id, char offsets) so we can compute grounding rate precisely.

I attached the two reference artifacts we shared with the customer (acme_benchmark_results.csv, prompt_set_v2.md) to this thread for traceability.

Thanks — let me know if any of these timelines are risky.
